item.title: Photocatalytic Biomass Valorization: Electronic Polarization Enables Oxygen Activation and Selective C─C Bond Cleavage
item.description:
Co active-site engineering and CF3-induced electronic polarization simultaneously help to endow g-C3N4 with enhanced interfacial electron transfer and efficient oxygen activation that can be perform under visible-light irradiation. The generated superoxide radicals (•O2 −) promote selective C─C bond cleavage of biomass-derived carbohydrates, enabling highly selective conversion into formic acid under mild aqueous conditions.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic valorization of biomass into value-added chemicals requires catalysts capable of simultaneously activating molecular oxygen and controlling C─C bond cleavage. In this work, we introduce an electronic polarization engineering strategy by integrating CF3-induced charge redistribution on Co active-site regulation in polymeric carbon nitride. It demonstrates that the as-prepared Co/g-C3N4-CF3 photocatalyst enables selective conversion of biomass-derived carbohydrates into formic acid under visible-light irradiation and mild aqueous conditions. Mechanistic investigations reveal that ─CF3 functionalization creates localized electronic polarization, while Co sites promote oxygen activation and facilitate the formation of superoxide radicals (•O2 −). Density functional theory calculations reveals that this electronic modulation lowers the energetic barrier for the key C─C bond cleavage step. Therefore, this work establishes a general framework for coupling electronic polarization with active-site engineering to help perform selective oxidation chemistry in solar-driven catalysis.

item.title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C19, C24, and C29 Terpenoids
item.description:
The terpenoid substrate analog 14-nor-FPP with a removed Me group and IPP were converted with oligoprenyl pyrophosphate synthases and di- or sesterterpene synthases to yield non-natural terpene analogs. In some cases, new cyclisation cascades were entered, leading to products with novel skeletons. Surprisingly, for some enzyme-substrate combinations, the removal of one carbon atom allows for incorporation of an additional isoprene unit.


ABSTRACT

The terpenoid substrate analog 14-nor-farnesyl pyrophosphate (14-nor-FPP), lacking the methyl group Me14, was synthesized and enzymatically elongated to 18-nor-geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (18-nor-GGPP) and 22-nor-geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (22-nor-GFPP) by GGPP synthase (GGPPS) and GFPP synthase (GFPPS), respectively. Downstream conversion with 20 diterpene synthases (DTSs) and 10 sesterterpene synthases (StTSs) yielded in total 24 new compounds. Surprisingly, in two cases the substrate analogs were converted by GGPPS and a DTS into nor-sesterterpenes (C24), while one combination of GFPPS and a StTS yielded a nor-triterpene (C29), demonstrating that the lack of just one carbon allows for extension with one more terpene unit than expected, in contrast to the strict product selectivity observed for GGPPS and GFPPS with normal FPP. For certain enzyme-substrate pairings, the altered reactivity caused by the absence of Me14 unveiled reaction pathways toward di- and sesterterpenes with unique frameworks, for which the mechanisms were investigated through DFT calculations. Absolute configurations of the obtained compounds were determined through chemical correlation with stereoselectively deuterated precursors or through a comparison of optical rotations to those of structurally related natural products containing Me18/Me22.

item.title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
item.description:
This work developed a chelator-engineered MSN platform that accommodates four distinct high-valent metal ions within a common nanoparticle architecture and enables their use as antibody-conjugated mass tags in multiplexed mass cytometry workflows.


ABSTRACT

Mass cytometry (MC) enables highly multiplexed single-cell protein analysis, but its full analytical potential remains constrained by the limited range of available mass tags. Here, we report deferoxamine-engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DFO-MSNs) for high-capacity loading of multiple underutilized high-valent metal ions within a common nanoparticle scaffold. DFO-MSNs accommodated Zr4+, Hf4+, Nb5+, and Ta5+ at approximately 104 metal atoms per nanoparticle, with high metal retention in physiological buffers. Following PEGylation and antibody (Ab) conjugation, the resulting Zr-, Nb-, Hf-, and Ta-based probes enabled antigen-specific detection of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by co-staining with commercial Maxpar reagents. Nb-, Hf-, and Ta-loaded MSN_CD8a probes resolved CD8a+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes at titers as low as 30 NPs/cell. In a 30-plex staining panel, Ta@MSN_CD25 resolved low-abundance CD25 hi CD127 lo Treg-like cells with apparent population recovery comparable to the corresponding Maxpar reagent, while consuming ca. 35-fold less Ab. Together, these results establish a modular strategy for incorporating underutilized high-valent metals into functional mass tags and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating MSN-based probes into multiplexed MC immunophenotyping workflows.

item.title: One Acceptor Core, Two Bright Pathways: CF3‐Substituted Triazines Achieve Highly Efficient Intermolecular Exciplexes and Intramolecular TADF
item.description:
A CF3-substituted triazine (T4) scaffold provides a unified platform for efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) through both inter- and intramolecular charge-transfer (CT) processes. Intermolecular CT-based exciplexes achieve record-high emission efficiency, while T4-3Cz exhibits strong three-photon absorption (3PA) and high photostability, highlighting multifunctional potential in optoelectronic and bioimaging applications.


ABSTRACT

Intermolecular charge-transfer (CT)-based exciplexes provide broad design flexibility through independent donor and acceptor selection, but often suffer from low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) due to limited orbital overlap. In contrast, intramolecular CT-based thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) systems can achieve high PLQYs through controlled donor-acceptor interactions, but generally require precise molecular design and substituent tuning. Here, we show that a CF3-substituted triazine scaffold (T4) serves as a unified molecular platform for achieving highly efficient emission through both intermolecular and intramolecular CT pathways. The CzCF3-substituted derivatives T4-2CzCF3 and T4-3CzCF3 formed highly emissive intermolecular exciplexes with mCBP, achieving PLQYs of 100%. Incorporation of stronger carbazole donors afforded T4-3Cz, which exhibited intramolecular CT-based TADF with PLQYs reaching 100% in solution and 100% in an mCBP-doped film. T4-3Cz also displayed near-infrared multiphoton absorption, with a two-photon absorption cross-section (σ2) of 80 GM at 780 nm and a three-photon absorption cross-section (σ3) of 2.94 × 10−80 cm6 s2 at 1210 nm. Furthermore, OLEDs based on the T4-3CzCF3 intermolecular exciplex and the intramolecular CT-based TADF emitter T4-3Cz exhibited efficient electroluminescent performance. These findings establish the T4 scaffold as a versatile molecular framework that integrates highly efficient intermolecular exciplex TADF, intramolecular CT-based TADF, multiphoton absorption, and OLED functionality.

item.title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
item.description:
Inspired by mitochondrial ATP synthase, pH-responsive COF nanochannel membranes achieve adaptive, directional ion transport without permanent asymmetry. Transmembrane pH polarization induces asymmetric charge regulation and internal electric fields, yielding ionic conductance from 0.4 to ∼1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100-fold NaCl gradient, these membranes deliver 20.2 W m− 2.


ABSTRACT

Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH-responsive PAN-supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH-dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100-fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m− 2. Experiments verify pH-dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH-mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

item.title: Promoting CO2 Electromethanation via Reverse H‐Spillover on Zeolite Y‐Confined CuO Nanoclusters
item.description:
Conventional CuO exhibits distributed product selectivity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction, while the encapsulation of CuO within the zeolite Y framework promotes the sequential hydrogenation of key intermediate *CO via reverse hydrogen spillover, thereby achieving a methane Faradaic efficiency exceeding 70% and a maximum partial current density of 656.1 mA cm−2.


ABSTRACT

The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (eCO2RR) presents a promising route for converting CO2 emissions into valuable products, with methane (CH4) being particularly attractive owing to its high energy density and infrastructure compatibility. However, selective CH4 formation via sequential *CO hydrogenation remains kinetically challenged by competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we encapsulate CuO nanoclusters within zeolite Y, where spatial confinement enables the uniform dispersion of CuO and enhances the reverse H-spillover (RHS)-mediated utilization of *H species generated on the zeolite support for sequential *CO hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH4 Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% ± 1.3% at 600 mA cm−2 and 65.6% ± 1.0% at 1000 mA cm−2. Experimental and theoretical studies show that H2O is preferentially activated on the zeolite support, generating *H species that are rapidly transferred to adjacent CuO via RHS for CO2 hydrogenation. Operando spectroscopic detection of CH4-related *OCH3/*CH x intermediates, together with DFT calculations, indicates that zeolite–CuO interactions favor *CO hydrogenation to *CHO over *CO dimerization, thereby promoting CH4 formation. This work establishes spatial confinement-coupled RHS as an effective strategy for regulating interfacial *H transfer and sequential hydrogenation in the eCO2RR process.

item.title: Rationale‐Guided and Iterative Learning for Redesigning a Highly Enantio‐ and Chemoselective Flavin‐Dependent Phenolic Hydroxylase
item.description:
Engineering biocatalysts for precise enantio- or chemoselectivity typically demands exhaustive effort, owing to the large number of screening iterations and the reliance on reliable mutational analysis. Here, we introduce a mechanistic insight-guided iterative learning workflow capable of simultaneously redesigning catalytic preferences of a flavin-dependent monooxygenase—achieved within just three rounds of single or double saturation mutagenesis per round.


ABSTRACT

Flavin-dependent monooxygenases (FDMOs) can catalyze C─H hydroxylation of phenolic compounds, yet the scope of their application has never been challenged beyond the hydroxylation of simple substrates nor explored for the ability to achieve selective hydroxylation. FDMO hydroxylation is often poorly controlled, yielding unstable, multiply hydroxylated products. Here, we used a mechanistic insight-guided iterative learning workflow to redesign the active site of p-hydroxyphenylacetate hydroxylase to expand its capability for chemo- and enantioselective control in the synthesis of (R)-norepinephrine. Within only three rounds of an engineering campaign, a DISD_LG variant that switched from (S)- to (R)-selective hydroxylation was obtained with excellent enantioselectivity (97.6%ee (R)). This variant also produced markedly fewer multiply hydroxylated products (<5% relative amount in the product mixture), indicating significant improvement in chemoselective control. The kinetic resolution was performed at a 20-mL scale (4 mM racemic substrate) and (R)-norepinephrine was obtained with 48.8% isolated yield and 96.2%ee (R). The molecular mechanisms underlying the enantio- and chemoselective control achieved by the DISD_LG variant were elucidated using molecular dynamics simulations. This work presents an enzyme engineering workflow to achieve kinetic resolution in combination with a controllable degree of hydroxylation, the aspects previously overlooked or underemphasized in FDMOs.

item.title: Pronounced Visible‐Light Cryptochirality Detection of Various Terpenoids via Helical Polyaromatic Capsules
item.description:
The efficient CD analysis of cryptochiral terpenoids is demonstrated by helical polyaromatic capsules upon simple encapsulation in water. The resultant host-guest complexes exhibit intense CD bands in the visible region (|Δε| up to ∼130 M−1 cm−1) derived from guest-induced host helicity. The use of two different capsules enables the chirality detection of diverse mono-, sesqui-, di-, and triterpenoids in the same way.


ABSTRACT

Cryptochirality refers to molecular chirality with undetectable/absent circular dichroism (CD) bands. Whereas there have been several host compounds capable of binding cryptochiral biosubstrates for their analysis, those with guest-induced CD activity in the visible region remain quite rare so far. We herein report the host-guest interaction-based CD analysis of various terpenoids using two different, helical polyaromatic capsules under ambient aqueous conditions. When one molecule of CD-inactive monoterpenoid, (–)-carvone, is quantitatively encapsulated within a CD-inactive capsule bearing a spheroidal cavity, the resultant host-guest complex displays pronounced CD bands in the range of 350–430 nm with a relatively high absolute molar circular dichroism value (i.e., |Δε| >80 M−1cm−1 at ∼390 nm), derived from the guest-induced host helicity. The chirality of other cryptochiral mono/sesquiterpenoids is also detected with similar efficiency (∼30–90 M−1cm−1). The enantiomeric excess (%ee) of d/l-mixtures of monoterpenoids can be determined with the helical cavity via comparative CD analysis. By the use of another larger capsule, di- and triterpenoids also induce its intense CD bands (up to ∼130 M−1cm−1) in the visible region upon encapsulation. The present study highlights the potential application of helical polyaromatic hosts to the facile cryptochiral analysis of a broad range of biosubstrates with intense CD output.

item.title: Topological Regioisomerism Enables Triplet–Triplet Energy‐Transfer for Reversible Dual Delayed Fluorescence–Phosphorescence Multicolor Afterglow
item.description:
Regioisomer-controlled host-guest engineering enables triplet-triplet energy transfer-driven dual delayed fluorescence-phosphorescence afterglow with fully reversible, temperature-dependent color switching (yellow → orange → red) from room temperature to cryogenic conditions.


ABSTRACT

Achieving concurrent thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) afterglow in purely organic systems remains elusive owing to limited control over triplet dynamics, competing decay pathways and unclear operational mechanisms. Reversible TADF/RTP modulation within a single host-guest system is challenging, hindering advances in color- and lifetime-tunable afterglow materials. To achieve this, we utilized regioisomerism as a structural topology control parameter in a host-guest platform to modulate triplet-triplet energy transfer (TTET), enabling the transition from exciplex TADF to dual TADF-RTP afterglow. The optimized system exhibits TADF-associated delayed emission with an intensity-weighted apparent lifetime of 617 ms, along with persistent RTP and ∼6.5-9.5 s afterglow. Temperature-dependent modulation of I TADF/I RTP ratio enables reversible cryogenic afterglow color evolution from yellow to orange and red through thermally regulated exciton redistribution.

item.title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
item.description:
Indolylphenylpropenone derivatives can be transformed into monocyclobutane and bicyclobutane products by tuning the irradiation wavelength. Blue light induces the formation of monocyclobutane via [2+2] cycloaddition of the vinyl groups, accompanied by a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation, while UV light activates the dearomatization of indole to afford bicyclobutane. Driven by photocycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibit pronounced photomechanical effects.


ABSTRACT

Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four-membered rings. However, controlling the regio- and stereo-selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo-photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation-wavelength-controlled, stepwise photo-induced topo-[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for (E)-1-(5-bromo-1H-indol-1-yl)-3-(3,5-difluorophenyl)prop-2-en-1-one (PEOBr5F35 ), this process proceeded via a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second-step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five-membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst-free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane-fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

item.title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
Synchronized acoustic and interfacial engineering enable rapid, homogeneous sodium compensation in thick hard carbon electrodes for a dry-air-processable manufacturing of high energy sodium-ion batteries.


ABSTRACT

Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium-ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high-loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound-driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F-rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry-air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid-electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide-temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry-air-compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

item.title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
item.description:
A visible light photocatalytic 1,2-boron migrative alkene homologation is achieved with tert-butylsulfonyl alkyl halides as a new type of vinylidene donors, producing structurally diverse remotely functionalized alkenes under mild conditions.


ABSTRACT

In contrast to well-established methods for vicinal di-functionalization of alkenes, remote di-functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron-directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless tert-butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3-difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β-Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra-thermodynamic 1,2-boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone-based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24-fluoro-25-hydroxyvitamin D3 analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one-carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

item.title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
item.description:
Interfacial electrochemical potential is modulated through descriptor-guided molecular grafting to facilitate sodium-ion transport in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs). Phenyltrimethoxysilane reduces the KPFM-derived surface potential mismatch by 87% and suppresses interfacial sodium-ion depletion. Lower interfacial migration barriers accompany these changes. The modified electrolyte exhibits enhanced ionic conductivity and enables stable cycling in all-solid-state sodium-metal batteries.


ABSTRACT

Sluggish ion transport kinetics between the ceramic and polymer phases remain a key challenge in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs), primarily due to a severe interfacial barrier arising from their intrinsic physicochemical incompatibility. Herein, molecular design-enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na3Zr2Si2PO12–poly(ethylene oxide) interface, based on a dual-axis screening guided by the electron-donating capability and molecular electronic asymmetry. By grafting different functional trimethoxysilanes from a targeted library onto the ceramic surface, the effect of the interfacial electrochemical potential on Na-ion transport is investigated, revealing a strong negative correlation with the ionic conductivity of CSEs. The CSE with the optimal grafting molecule (phenyltrimethoxysilane) reduces the potential mismatch by 87% and lowers the Na-ion migration barrier, thereby boosting Na-ion conductivity by two orders of magnitude. All-solid-state sodium-metal batteries using this CSE show boosted electrochemical performance with a high capacity of 91.8 mAh g−1 delivered at 5 C and retain ∼99% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a screening framework for reducing interfacial potential mismatch and addressing the long-standing ion-transport bottleneck across ceramic–polymer interfaces in CSEs.

item.title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li+ Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
item.description:
Amino-functionalized UiO66-NH2 triggers p-π conjugation and strengthened LMCT, weakening Li+-FSI− pairing to accelerate Li+ migration. The composite SPE achieves good electrochemical performance and stable cycling for high-loading solid-state lithium metal batteries.


ABSTRACT

Sluggish Li+ transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)-based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li+-FSI− association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino-functionalized UiO66-NH2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron-donating ─NH2 groups induce p-π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)-related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr-O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino-associated modulation of local O-centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li+-FSI− interactions, and facilitates Li+ migration. U6NP delivers a room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10−3 S cm−1, a Li+ transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm−2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g−1 initially and 120.9 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH2-induced p-π conjugation-enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF-reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high-loading solid-state lithium metal batteries.

item.title: Phosphate‐Modulated Asymmetric Copper Catalysis for Photochemical Enantioselective S‐Benzylation of Sulfenamides
item.description:
A visible-light-driven copper/PyOx/phosphate catalytic platform enables asymmetric radical benzylation of sulfenamides via three distinct radical-generation pathways, delivering enantioenriched S-stereogenic sulfilimines under mild conditions. The bulky phosphate anion acts as a multifunctional secondary-sphere regulator that modulates the copper coordination environment and stabilizes key intermediates, collectively ensuring high reactivity and enantioselectivity.


ABSTRACT

S-stereogenic sulfilimines constitute valuable S(IV)-based scaffolds widely encountered in chiral ligands, pharmaceuticals, and bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective construction remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a versatile copper catalytic platform assembled from a chiral pyridine-oxazoline (PyOx) ligand, a bulky phosphate, and a Cu(I) salt to generate the active catalyst. This chiral copper/PyOx/phosphate system accommodates three mechanistically distinct radical-generation pathways upon light irradiation, encompassing single-electron transfer reduction of Katritzky salts, proton-coupled electron transfer decarboxylation of carboxylic acids, and hydrogen atom transfer activation of toluene derivatives. Such flexibility enables efficient asymmetric radical benzylation of readily accessible sulfenamides under mild conditions. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the phosphate anion serves a multifunctional role, modulating the copper coordination sphere and stabilizing key copper–sulfur intermediates, which collectively boost both reactivity and enantioselectivity. The methodology delivers enantioenriched sulfilimines with broad substrate scope and operational simplicity. This work establishes a general blueprint for integrating multiple radical-generation modes into a single stereocontrolled catalytic framework, demonstrating that rational modulation of the secondary coordination sphere can unlock new possibilities in stereoselective radical chemistry.
